title: WPCRL/270/2013 of SMT POOJA MATHUR and OTHERS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL

Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
Paritosh Mathur (husband) and Geetanjali Singh
(wife) are present, in person and they are duly identified by
their respective Advocates - Mr. Shailendra Nauriyal and Mr.
D.C.S. Rawat.
Vide order dated 29.05.2013, parties were directed
to appear before the Mediation Centre of this Court to explore
the possibility of amicable settlement. Learned Mediator
(Additional Registrar I) has reported that parties have settled
their differences amicably.
Parties, present before this Court, submit that they
have settled their differences amicably and now, both of them
are living together as husband and wife and would pay utmost
respect to each other and to their parents.
Respondent no. 2 Geetanjali further submits that in
view of amicable settlement between parties, she does not want
to prosecute the petitioners.

2
Learned counsel for the parties submit that in view
of the amicable settlement between parties, no useful purpose
would be served in keeping the criminal proceedings alive.
Honíble Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs.
State of Punjab reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 has opined that
criminal proceedings arising out of matrimonial dispute can be
quashed, if parties have arrived at mutual settlement to restore
the peace and harmony between them.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties,
parties, in person, and going through the material available on
record, I am satisfied that matter has been settled between the
parties amicably and no useful purpose would be served in
keeping the prosecution alive, therefore, present petition is
allowed. Impugned FIR and all the proceedings pursuant
thereto are quashed.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 28.06.2013
SKS
